answer.text: Listing securities on an exchange via a public offer
Issue of securities to a select group of persons (fewer than 200), neither a rights issue nor a public issue

explanation.text: The Logic: Private placement is defined as an issue of securities to a select group of persons. It is made to fewer than 200 persons and is neither a rights issue nor a public issue. The Trap: Public offers, IPOs and employee stock options are distinct issue routes. The defining test for private placement is the select group and the sub-200 limit, not the type of investor. Note: Reserve QIB wording for QIP items; do not describe private placement as an issuance to qualified investors generically, since that risks confusion with QIB/QIP.
